works.abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge‐like pore structure, a narrow pore‐size distribution, and a high β ‐phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca 2+ rejection and a Na + /Ca 2+ separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an “electrostatic–piezoelectric synergistic enhancement” separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

works.title: Microporous N-Boc-functionalized poly(isatin fluorene) thin-film composite membranes for hydrocarbon separations
works.abstract: Organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) offers an energy efficient approach to hydrocarbon fractionation, but achieving high molecular selectivity while maintaining sufficient permeance remains challenging. Here, N -tert-butyloxycarbonyl-functionalized poly(isatin fluorene) (PIF-Boc) was investigated as selective-layer material for composite OSN membranes. The rigid cardo architecture contributes to substantial free volume by disrupting efficient chain packing. Fractional free volumes estimated from experimental density were 0.233 and 0.196 for PIF and PIF-Boc, respectively, with molecular dynamics simulations further supporting substantial free volume in both polymers. Boc functionalization improved thin film processability in chlorinated solvents while retaining good mechanical properties, enabling solution coating of PIF-Boc onto porous polyacrylonitrile supports. The coating solvent and polymer concentration strongly affected membrane morphology and separation performance, providing tunable permeance-selectivity characteristics. Chloroform-derived membranes generally favored higher permeance, whereas 1,1,2-trichloroethane (TCE) produced more uniform coatings and higher selectivity. Using a nine-component synthetic crude oil feed, the optimized TCE-derived membrane maintained relatively stable permeance and increasing selectivity up to approximately 45 bar, achieving separation factors of 2.63 for n -octane/iso-cetane and 2.16 for toluene/1,3,5-triisopropylbenzene. A separation factor of 1.28 was achieved for 1-methylnaphthalene/decalin. Benchmarking against six commercial OSN membranes using the same feed demonstrated competitive permeance-selectivity performance. These results establish PIF-Boc as a promising and tunable membrane platform for energy-efficient hydrocarbon fractionation.

works.title: Vertically aligned dual-channel metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes for gas separation
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering
State Key Laboratory of Materials-Oriented Chemical Engineering
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
works.abstract: The nanostructure of two-dimensional (2D) membranes is crucial for their separation performance. However, in conventional 2D membranes, guest species unavoidably permeate through tortuous pathways, resulting in effective transport lengths that are orders of magnitude greater than the membrane thickness. Here, we propose vertically aligned metal-organic framework (MOF) nanosheet membranes featuring bimodal porosity: intrinsic lateral pores within the MOF nanosheets and interlamellar pores between them, forming an ultralow-tortuosity, dual-sieving channel system for efficient gas separation. Despite their relatively large thickness, the resulting MOF nanosheet membranes exhibit a high H 2 permeance of 16673 GPU (up to an order of magnitude higher than the reported average) along with an H 2 /CO 2 separation selectivity of 325 under standardized atmospheric Wicke-Kallenbach conditions (zero transmembrane partial pressure difference). This work not only provides a promising membrane platform for H 2 /CO 2 separation but also offers an alternative strategy for constructing next-generation molecular sieve membranes.

works.title: Revisiting the Characteristics and Performance of Acid-Treated Polyamide Membranes: Fundamental Insights and Implications
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

Shenzhen Machinery Institute Architectural Design Co Ltd , ,
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology , , ,
Tsinghua University, Shenzhen International Graduate School , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Acid treatment of polyamide reverse osmosis (RO) and nanofiltration (NF) membranes is a commonly used approach for membrane cleaning and modification. However, there are contradictory observations on the effects of acid treatment in the current literature. Herein, we systematically characterized the changes in the physicochemical properties of both RO and NF membranes under different acid treatment conditions. Both acid-treated RO and NF membranes exhibited similar surface physicochemical characteristics compared with their respective original membranes. Interestingly, the acid-treated RO membrane showed a nearly doubled water permeance while maintaining high salt rejection. During the acid treatment, the fully aromatic RO membrane underwent selective removal of monomers/oligomers from the bottom region of its asymmetric polyamide layer, as evidenced by the appearance of N-rich molecules in the acid rinsing solution and the increased O/N ratio of the polyamide bottom side. At the same time, the O/N ratio of the polyamide top surface was not affected. In comparison, no release of monomers/oligomers was detected during the acid treatment of the semiaromatic NF membrane. Correspondingly, the NF membrane had a comparable water permeance before and after acid treatment. In the current study, the acid-treated RO membrane demonstrated improved water permeance and stable rejection of NaCl and several micropollutants, suggesting that acid treatment could be used as a polishing strategy to improve the performance of RO membranes for high-efficiency water treatment.

works.title: Climbing the green ladder - toward a greener synthesis of polymers of intrinsic microporosity for separation membranes
works.abstract: Polymer membranes are materials that have a broad applicability for gas or liquid separation. Among them the polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIMs) and especially PIM-1 are a promising material class. Its conventional synthesis relies on base-catalyzed polycondensation conducted in petrochemical solvents, raising concerns regarding toxicity, sustainability and environmental impact. To address these limitations, we systematically evaluated the synthesis of the polymer in a wide range of greener solvent systems in combination with both the typical fluor-containing PIM-1 comonomer along with the less hazardous, chlorine-containing comonomer. Through comprehensive solvent screening and optimization of reaction conditions, a greener reaction protocol that yields PIM-1 with molecular characteristics comparable to those produced via the standard process in dimethylformamide was established. Subsequent gas-separation and organic solvent nanofiltration testing of the resulting membrane, performed on both dense films and thin-film composite membranes, demonstrated permeation and selectivity values fully comparable to those of PIM-1 synthesized via the classical route. This study highlights that greener solvents and less toxic monomers can effectively replace conventional reagents without compromising polymer quality or membrane performance, thereby providing a viable, greener pathway for producing high-performance PIM materials.

works.title: Advanced Membrane Processes for the Removal of Anthelmintics, Neonicotinoids and Their Mixtures: Retention Mechanisms and Effects on Ecotoxicity
works.abstract: Veterinary anthelmintics and neonicotinoid insecticides in aquatic environments pose challenges for conventional wastewater treatment. Six commercial ultrafiltration (UF), nanofiltration (NF), and reverse osmosis (RO) membranes were evaluated for the rejection of three veterinary anthelmintics (albendazole, febantel, and mebendazole) and three neonicotinoid insecticides (acetamiprid, clothianidin, and thiacloprid). The compounds were tested individually and as a six-component mixture in demineralized and model water. After 3 h, rejection of the individual compounds was at least 92.9% with the tight NF membrane ESNA1-LF-LD and 94.1% with the RO membrane ESPA4. Neonicotinoid rejection by the UF membrane did not exceed 9.2%. In the six-component mixture, ESNA1-LF-LD rejected 87.9–94.9% of neonicotinoids and 90.1% to >99.9% of anthelmintics. The RO membranes (XLE and ESPA4) rejected 89.8–94.8% of neonicotinoids and 92.5% to >99.9% of anthelmintics. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicated possible interactions between anthelmintics and the membranes. At the highest sample volume fraction tested, the untreated mixture caused 63.6% inhibition of Vibrio fischeri bioluminescence in demineralized water and 86.8% in model water. No inhibition was detected in the XLE or ESPA4 permeates. Rejection depended on membrane selectivity, compound properties, and water matrix. Combining chemical measurements with ecotoxicity assays provided a broader assessment of membrane treatment performance.

works.title: Harnessing Weak Intermolecular Interactions for Efficient PFOA Capture in a Fluorine-Rich Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Membrane
institutions: New York University Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) , , Saadiyat Island , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

works.title: Programmable Stepped Homojunction COF Membranes for High‑Efficiency Light‑Driven Ion Pumping via Photo‐Conformational Coupling
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Tropic Ocean Engineering Materials and Materials Evaluation, School of Materials Science and Engineering Hainan University Haikou People's Republic of China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Bioinspired light‐driven ion pumps convert solar energy into directional ionic flux, yet low photocarrier separation efficiency and high ion migration barriers within confined nanochannels severely restrict their performance. A covalent organic framework (COF) homojunction membrane is constructed via assembling exfoliated nanosheets with accurately regulated protonation levels. Such modular assembly produces staggered band alignment without changing framework compositions, which facilitates efficient charge separation and oriented carrier migration under light irradiation to form an intrinsic electric field for ion pumping. Different from common photovoltaic effects, photoexcitation induces reversible torsional relaxation of COF skeletons to directly weaken ion‐pore wall interactions and cut ion transport kinetic barriers, which is validated by molecular dynamics simulations and in situ FTIR characterization. Benefiting from this synergistic photo‐conformational coupling, optimized homojunction membranes realize improved charge separation and decreased transport resistance. The material achieves 219% higher photocurrent and 324% larger power density than uniformly protonated counterparts, and enables uphill ion transport against a tenfold concentration gradient. A programmable fabrication route is thus proposed for COF homojunction ion pumps, and photoinduced framework torsion is confirmed as a key factor to reduce ion transport barriers.

works.title: Waste-Derived Zwitterionic Bacterial Cellulose Membranes with Enhanced Silica and Scaling Control for Sustainable Nanofiltration Pretreatment
institutions: Khalifa University of Science and Technology
Khalifa University of Science and Technology , , , P.O. Box 127788,
works.abstract: Abstract Bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes were engineered via kombucha fermentation with the incorporation of polyethylene glycol (PEG-600 and PEG-1000, 1–2%, w/v) to tailor pore formation and enhance structural stability. Subsequently, the BC membrane was functionalized with chitosan polyampholyte (CPA) to introduce zwitterionic properties for fouling mitigation. The incorporation of 2% PEG-1000 enhances BC production and mechanical properties, with elongation increasing from 20.3% to 49.7%. The zwitterionic modification leads to reduced pore size and altered surface morphology of BC membrane. The zwitterionic CPA-BC membrane exhibits effective pretreatment performance, achieving accumulated removals of 45% for soluble silica, 35% for calcium (Ca2+), and 19% for sulfate (SO42–), while maintaining a stable flux of 20 L m–2 h–1 over 17 h. CPA-BC pretreatment mitigates surface fouling of the commercial nanofiltration (NF) membrane, as evidenced by optical coherence tomography (OCT) and digital image processing, which reveal reduced surface coverage from 99.4% to 64.8%. This contributes to reducing the rapid flux decline observed with pretreatment, from 42 L m–2 h–1 at 2 h to 29 L m–2 h–1 at 17 h, compared to a rapid decline to 7 L m–2 h–1 within 2 h without pretreatment. The findings demonstrate the technical potential of waste-derived zwitterionic BC membranes to offer an effective and sustainable pretreatment strategy for controlling silica fouling and scaling, enabling improved stability and performance of desalination systems.

works.title: Steroid Hormone Transport and Adsorption Energy in Non‐functionalized Cylindrical Nanopores: Insights From Molecular Dynamics
works.abstract: Hydrophobic and uncharged micropollutants, such as steroid hormones, pass through nanofiltration membranes due to adsorption to the membrane polymers and gradual diffusion through the active layer. The adsorption strength is difficult to quantify as the realistic pores are complex, with sections of varying diameter, roughness/tortuosity, and functional group density hampering both computational and experimental investigations. This study employs molecular dynamics to investigate hormone adsorption and how it affects transport inside structurally uniform single‐walled carbon nanotube pores with controlled diameters (0.81−3.66 nm). Results show that, with 1.9 nm diameter pores, the free energy change of adsorption (Δ G ads ) for 17β‐estradiol − a potent female sex hormone − is as high as −76 kJ/mol, consistent with the hormone's restricted movement under water flow. The adsorption strength varies with hormone type and pore diameter – however, the clogging effect rather than Δ G ads dictates the hormone movement speed. Background solvent when introduced at high concentrations can have pronounced effects. Ethanol at a molar percentage exceeding 36% forms a ‘buffer’ layer between the pore wall and hormone, reducing Δ G ads and enhancing hormone mobility. This study differentiates adsorption from other removal mechanisms, such as retention, to advance the understanding of adsorption−transport relationship in nanofiltration for selectivity.

works.title: Heat stable salts in amine-based gas treatment: Formation mechanisms, impacts, reclamation, and hybrid mitigation strategies
works.abstract: Heat stable salts (HSS) are persistent, non-regenerable salts formed when protonated amines associate with acid anions that are not removed under normal regeneration conditions. Their accumulation reduces the fraction of active amine and may impair acid-gas absorption, while their effects on corrosion and foaming depend on anion identity, solvent formulation, co-contaminants, and operating conditions. This review critically examines HSS formation mechanisms, physicochemical characteristics, analytical determination, operational impacts, and conventional and emerging reclamation technologies. Solution purging, neutralization, thermal reclamation, and ion exchange are compared with electrodialysis, bipolar membrane electrodialysis, adsorption, electrosorption, electromagnetic separation, nanofiltration, and hybrid processes in terms of removal performance, amine retention, chemical and energy requirements, regeneration, fouling, waste generation, and industrial readiness. Ion exchange remains one of the most established options for deep HSS removal, with reported efficiencies of 77–97%; however, resin capacity loss, regenerant demand, and spent-regenerant management remain important constraints. Membrane-based technologies offer potential for selective removal and reduced chemical consumption, but their performance depends on anion-specific transport and rejection, amine concentration, operating conditions, and membrane properties. To address the need for process integration, an ion-exchange/anion-adsorptive-membrane side-stream configuration is proposed for lean-amine purification. This conceptual design aims to combine primary HSS removal with membrane polishing while limiting amine loss. Laboratory- and pilot-scale validation, together with techno-economic assessment, is required to establish its performance and industrial feasibility.

works.title: Removal of Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals from Water Using Advanced Oxidation Processes (AOPs) and Ozonation
works.abstract: This study evaluates the nanofiltration (NF) and ozonation of the resulting concentrates for six target compounds: N,N-diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET), 3-(4-methylbenzylidene)camphor (4MBC), triclosan (TRC), carbamazepine (CBZ), estrone (E1), and estradiol (E2). The experiments were performed on surface water. The supplied endpoint data showed strongly compound-dependent membrane behavior. NF removal ranged from 33 to 75% for most detected compounds. Ozonation of the NF concentrate was highly effective for CBZ, TRC, 4MBC, E1, and E2 at both nominal doses, while DEET remained comparatively resistant. The nominal dose of ozone increased from 150 to 300 mg/L. The results demonstrate the potential of coupling dense-membrane separation with oxidative retentate treatment.

works.title: Ion-Capture Electrodialysis for Simultaneous Adsorptive Capture of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Brackish Water Desalination
institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are anthropogenic contaminants present in natural waters worldwide, including some brackish waters. Ion-capture electrodialysis (IC-ED) captures contaminants of interest while permeating nontargeted salts. We hypothesize that IC-ED is a viable strategy for simultaneous PFAS removal and brackish water desalination because the anionic charge, bulky structure, and hydrophobic properties of PFAS could interact favorably with anion exchange membranes (AEMs), facilitating PFAS removal. Accordingly, our primary objective was to determine the feasibility of simultaneous PFAS removal and desalination using IC-ED. Further, incorporating fluorous groups into materials is an emerging strategy to improve PFAS removal. Therefore, our secondary objective was to investigate the role of AEM modification via C–H fluoroalkylation on PFAS capture during IC-ED. Results showed that during IC-ED, up to 85.8% PFAS capture was observed after 24 h (73.6% after approximately 8 h), and ≥89% desalination was achieved after approximately 8 h. Further, net PFAS desorption from AEMs during IC-ED was not detectable, and AEMs were effectively regenerated (&gt;95%) using a chemical-based desorption approach. Energy consumption for IC-ED was on the same order of magnitude as reverse osmosis, but more work is needed to optimize IC-ED for energy efficiency. Comparing the performance of unmodified and modified AEMs showed that the modified AEMs enabled limited to moderate (p &lt; 0.05) improvement in PFAS capture during IC-ED, moderately lower energy consumption, and significantly faster PFAS capture (19.2–39.5% higher rate constant) under batch conditions compared with unmodified AEMs. The generally higher PFAS capture and faster PFAS sorption kinetics by the modified AEMs may be partly attributed to fluorophilic interactions. This work establishes a proof-of-concept for simultaneous PFAS capture and desalination and demonstrates that membrane physicochemical properties affect PFAS capture during IC-ED.

works.title: Progress in Preparation of Hydrophilic Polymer Brush-Grafted UiO-66-NH 2 Mixed Matrix Membranes and Their Antifouling Seawater Desalination Performance
works.abstract: Nowadays, the primary dilemma facing humanity is the gradual depletion of freshwater resources. In recent years, global warming and the rapid growth of population and industrialization have intensified this contradiction, and seawater desalination is undoubtedly the optimal solution to this problem. Currently, the most mainstream seawater desalination technology worldwide is reverse osmosis. According to data from the Global Water Intelligence, seawater reverse osmosis accounts for more than 70% of global seawater desalination capacity. Membrane fouling is one of the main limitations of reverse osmosis, including organic fouling, inorganic scaling, and colloidal fouling. Fouling leads to flux decline, increased energy consumption, shortened membrane lifespan, and requires frequent use of chemical cleaning agents, further increasing costs and environmental burden. This paper reviews membrane preparation methods and compares the performance of modified MMMs and TFNs with their respective pristine membranes. From the data, MMMs and TFNs demonstrate superior performance and are fully capable of serving as primary membrane materials for seawater desalination. Research has found that polymers are undoubtedly the most suitable for seawater desalination research. The general process involves first synthesizing UiO-66-NH 2 nanoparticles, then performing polymer brush grafting modification, followed by preparation into mixed matrix membranes and thin-film nanocomposite membranes, and then conducting performance tests on the two different membranes. Polymer brush-grafted UiO-66-NH 2 shows significant advantages in antifouling and desalination. However, long-term stability and cost control remain the core challenges facing the industrialization of this technology.

works.title: Integrated Membrane–Solar Systems for Zero Liquid Discharge in Inland Desalination
institutions: Brega Petroleum Marketing Company, Tripoli, Libya
Gas Processing Center, Qatar University, Doha P.O. Box 2713, Qatar
Central Laboratories Unit, Qatar University, Doha P.O. Box 2713, Qatar
works.abstract: Inland desalination plants produce reject brine that is difficult to dispose of when there is no access to the sea. This study evaluates the combination of two-stage reverse osmosis (RO) with solar evaporation as a pathway toward zero liquid discharge (ZLD) for inland desalination, based on twelve months of field measurements in Tripoli, Libya. The evaporation rate of RO reject brine was measured in covered evaporators at depths of 1–4 cm, and single-stage and two-stage RO configurations were simulated with the DuPont WAVE software. The annual mean evaporation rate was 2.71 kg/m2/day, ranging from 0.70 kg/m2/day in December to 5.25 kg/m2/day in June. The two-stage configuration raised the total water recovery from 75.2% to 94.0%. For 6 h of daily operation, this reduced the brine volume from 1980 to 480 L/day (75.8%) and the estimated evaporation pond area from 730.6 to 177.1 m2. These results show that increasing RO recovery before solar evaporation can considerably reduce the land needed for brine disposal at inland desalination plants.

works.title: Design and evaluation of a portable multifunctional nanofibrous membrane with photocatalytic activity for water purification: from in silico to in vitro
works.abstract: Access to clean, safe drinking water is a vital global priority, demanding rapid, reliable, and portable on-demand purification technologies for emergency response, field operations, and remote communities. In this study, a multifunctional portable membrane (designated as NFi) composed of electrospun nylon-6 functionalised with zinc oxide nanoparticles (N-6@ZnO) and polycaprolactone integrated with graphene oxide (PCL@GO) was engineered for high-performance water treatment. Molecular modeling-utilizing Density Functional Theory with dispersion corrections (DFT-D) and Monte Carlo (MC) adsorption locator simulations-elucidated the robust energetic affinity and favourable thermodynamic interactions governing the N-6@ZnO/PCL@GO hybrid architecture, evidenced by negative adsorption energies. Structurally, the electrospun fibrous network features mean pore dimensions of 627.3 nm (pristine N-6/PCL) to 793.0 nm (N-6@ZnO/PCL@GO), classifying the matrix geometrically within the microfiltration regime while providing interconnected mass-transfer channels. Under an operating pressure of 2 bar, the resulting N-6@ZnO/PCL@GO membrane demonstrated an outstanding pure water flux of 2,037 L·m−2·h−1 (pure water permeability of 1,019 L⋅m−2⋅h−1⋅bar−1), representing a ∼40% enhancement over the pristine N-6/PCL membrane (1,455 L⋅m−2⋅h−1⋅bar−1). Concurrently, the membrane demonstrated remarkable separation and degradation capabilities, achieving 99.2% rejection/photodegradation of methylene blue (MB) and total elimination (100% bactericidal efficacy) of both Gram-negative (Escherichia coli) and Gram-positive (Enterococcus) pathogens under visible/UV light irradiation via synergistic photocatalytic ROS generation and contact killing. These findings establish that combining nanofibrous electrospun scaffolding with photocatalytically active nano-inclusions yields an efficient, low-resistance, and highly portable platform for rapid water decontamination.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Infographic titled 'Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process-Based Assessment of Seawater Desalination Plant Operational Performance,' with three color-coded sections: Research Analysis, Research Results, and Conclusions. This work presents a performance evaluation framework for seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination plants, using the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) to assess the operational performance of the Chatt El Hilal seawater desalination plant, located at Beni Saf (western Algeria). The study develops a desalination-specific criteria tree comprising 5 main factors and 18 subcriteria, structured to reflect degradation mechanisms specific to SWRO operation, together with a four-state rating rubric used to score each subcriterion. Criterion weights were derived using FAHP based on the judgment of a five-member expert panel, and operational scores were computed for five illustrative scenarios reflecting different plant conditions. The results show that the model is sensitive to changes in individual criteria and produces composite scores consistent with the severity of the conditions specified in each scenario, illustrating its potential as a decision-support tool for identifying critical subsystems and prioritizing maintenance actions. The performance scores (Sp) obtained, ranging from 3.74 to 10, are consistent with the state of the facility as qualitatively described in each scenario.

works.title: Heterodyne-Detected Sum-Frequency Generation Spectroscopy at Two-Dimensional Material–Water Interfaces: A Practical Guide
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research
works.abstract: Water at two-dimensional (2D) material surfaces plays a central role in catalysis, electrochemistry, and nanofluidics. Molecular-level insights into their structure and dynamics at buried 2D material/water interfaces are essential for understanding interfacial mechanisms and guiding the design of functional systems. Heterodyne-detected sum-frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy provides a direct probe of interfacial water, but its quantitative application to 2D materials has been limited by the difficulty of extracting the intrinsic interfacial molecular response, which requires accurate phase measurement and rigorous Fresnel-factor corrections. In multilayer 2D material geometries, this challenge is further compounded by nanoconfined water trapped between the 2D material and its supporting material, the finite nonlinear response of the 2D material itself, and its crystallographic symmetry, all of which modulate both the amplitude and phase of the measured signal. Here, we present a practical protocol that enables robust, quantitative HD-SFG measurements at thin-film 2D material/water interfaces by explicitly accounting for thin-film interference and nanoconfined water as well as the intrinsic nonlinear response of the 2D material. Using SiO2-supported hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) thin films as a model system, we systematically investigate the roles of nanoconfined water, film thickness, crystallographic orientation, and substrate effects, demonstrating quantitative and selective probing of interfacial water at hBN surfaces. We further establish an experimentally implementable phase-retrieval and Fresnel-correction scheme, based on an in situ hBN/D2O reference, that yields the intrinsic Im χyyz(2)spectrum of interfacial water at the hBN/water interface, independent of film thickness and crystal orientation. Moreover, this approach provides a strategy for probing nanoconfined water by selecting appropriate thin-film materials, paving the way for future studies of interfacial water under nanoscale confinement. This methodology establishes a general framework for interpreting HD-SFG spectra at 2D material/water interfaces and is broadly applicable to a wide range of 2D materials, including membrane systems, as well as polymer thin films, and complements existing thin-film SFG treatments by extending Fresnel-factor engineering to phase-resolved HD-SFG at 2D material/liquid interfaces.

works.title: Process Integrated Comparative Assessment of Conventional and On-Purpose 1,3-Butadiene Production: Energy, Separation, and Decarbonization Perspectives
works.abstract: Abstract 1,3-Butadiene (1,3-BD) is one of the most commercially significant petrochemical monomers, underpinning the global synthetic rubber and plastics industries. Historically, it has been produced primarily as a byproduct of steam cracking of naphtha; however, the transition of global ethylene production toward lighter, shale gas-derived feedstocks has resulted in considerable strain in its sustainable availability (Samsudin, I. B.; et al.Chem. Asian J2020, 15, 24, 4199−4214.). This review provides a process-integrated comparative assessment of conventional and on-purpose 1,3-butadiene production technologies, evaluated through the lenses of energy consumption, separation performance, and decarbonization potential. The conventional C4 extraction route and its state-of-the-art NMP based separation technology are critically analyzed alongside a spectrum of on-purpose alternatives, including oxidative dehydrogenation (ODH) of n-butenes, direct dehydrogenation of n-butane, ethanol-to-butadiene (ETB) processes, butanediol dehydration routes, and emerging electrochemical pathways ( Brencio, C.; et al.Int. J. Hydrogen Energy2022, 47, 50, 21375−21390.,Teh, W. J.; et al.Nat. Catal.2024, 7, 12, 1382–1393.,Mantingh, J.; et al.Sep. Purif. Technol2021, 267, 118656.). Key findings indicate that while conventional steam cracking coupled with optimized extractive distillation remains the most energy-mature technology, its dependence on fossil feedstock and substantial greenhouse gas footprint makes it increasingly incompatible with net-zero industrial targets ( Cespi, D.; et al.Green Chem2016, 18, 6, 1625−1638.,Maga, D.; et al.Chem. Ing. Tech.2024, 96, 5, 688–697.). Among on-purpose routes, the biobased ETB one-step (Lebedev) process and 1,3-butanediol dehydration exhibit the most promising decarbonization profiles, despite current cost-competitiveness challenges relative to fossil-derived butadiene ( Camacho, C. E. C.; et al.J. Clean. Prod2022, 374, 133963.,Janssens, P.; et al.Ind. Eng. Chem. Res2025, 64, 45, 21571–21587.). Future process integration strategies, including heat pump-assisted distillation, dividing wall columns, membrane reactor technologies, and renewable energy coupling, are identified as essential levers for achieving technically and economically viable low-carbon butadiene supply chains. This review presents a unique cross-route analytical framework that simultaneously addresses energy demand, separation technology, C4 extraction solvent performance comparison, and life cycle carbon footprint across the full spectrum of 1,3-butadiene production routes from conventional steam cracking to biobased ethanol conversion, butanediol dehydration, furfural-derived pathways, natural gas integration, and the recently reported electrochemical route.

works.title: Electroconductive Membrane Bioreactor (EMBR) for Simultaneous Emerging Contaminants Removal and Fouling Control
works.abstract: Abstract The persistent presence of emerging contaminants, including antibiotics and endocrine-disrupting compounds, in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and public health challenges. Standalone biological and electrochemical advanced oxidation processes each face significant limitations in effectively removing emerging contaminants. Therefore, integrating these technologies offers a promising approach to bridging performance gaps and enhancing overall contaminant removal in wastewater treatment. This study develops an integrated electroconductive membrane bioreactor (EMBR) that combines a bioreactor with a side-stream electroconductive membrane, enabling efficient removal of emerging contaminants and effective control of fouling. It details the fabrication and application of laser-induced graphene (LIG)-incorporated polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) composite electroconductive membranes (LIGPVDF ECMs) prepared via the nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) method. The membranes were integrated into the EMBR and assessed for their ability to remove and degrade amoxicillin (AMX), bisphenol A (BPA), and ciprofloxacin (CIP). Despite their ultrafiltration pore sizes, the LIGPVDF membranes achieved up to ∼99% removal at low applied voltages (1–3 V), comparable to nanofiltration membranes. The performance was also evaluated across different pH conditions in crossflow filtration mode using synthetic wastewater. High removal was attributed to electrochemical oxidation, electro-adsorption, and Donnan exclusion. In addition to pollutant removal, cathodic LIGPVDF potentials reduced fouling to 13% flux decline (vs &gt;50% anodic), while electrocleaning restored ∼91% flux from bioreactor effluent, outperforming DI cleaning (∼68%). The findings provide a pathway for developing hybrid, energy-efficient treatment technologies that target emerging contaminants under environmentally relevant conditions.

works.title: A Proposed Phenomenological Material–Energy Scaling Framework for Recovery-Constrained Solvent Sustainability
works.abstract: Solvents constitute a major material and environmental burden in pharmaceutical manufacturing, yet sustainability assessment is still largely based on proportional metrics such as Process Mass Intensity (PMI) and aggregated life-cycle indicators. Building on our previously published solvent-centric sustainability framework, which integrated PMI, circular PMI (cPMI), Global Warming Potential (GWP), and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) for solvent-focused process assessment, the present study develops a phenomenological material–energy scaling formulation for recovery-constrained solvent sustainability. The proposed relationship is formulated as a testable phenomenological scaling framework, with its present scope limited to a system-specific relationship rather than a universal physical law. The framework represents the total sustainability burden, L(η), as a combination of a material-driven contribution and a recovery-associated nonlinear contribution: L(η) = c + kM(η) + β[ηn/(1 − η)], where M(η) is solvent material intensity, η is the recovery fraction, c is an intercept, k is a material-impact coefficient, β represents system-specific recovery-associated sensitivity, and n is a phenomenological recovery exponent. A dimensionless form is: L* = c* + αM* + λ[ηn/(1 − η)], where L* = L/L0, M* = M/M0, c* = c/L0, α = kM0/L0, and λ = β/L0. The nonlinear coordinate, Φ(η;n) = ηn/(1 − η), is used as a practical representation of recovery-associated asymptotic behaviour rather than as a first-principles thermodynamic equation. The parameters β, λ, and n are therefore expected to depend on the solvent, process configuration, recovery technology, operating conditions, response being measured, and system boundary. A seven-record pharmaceutical case-study dataset was used to examine the linear material relationship, the proposed nonlinear recovery coordinate, and an extended material–recovery interaction. Across the records, solvent mass decreases from 150 to 45 kg·kg−1 API as recovery increases from 30% to 92%, while energy use decreases from 520 to 380 MJ·kg−1 API. The linear model explains most of the observed variation (R2 = 0.979), whereas adding the nonlinear recovery term provides only a small improvement (R2 = 0.981), is penalized by information criteria, and gives an exponent at its imposed upper limit. An extended interaction model gives a closer fit to the seven observations, but its five-parameter structure relative to only seven observations does not support claims of independent predictive performance. These results therefore provide a basis for treating the proposed formulation as a testable phenomenological scaling hypothesis, rather than as evidence for a universal material–energy law. A complementary step-resolved analysis examines how solvent-related material and environmental burdens are distributed across individual process operations and how recovery may shift the balance between material use and recovery-associated energy requirements. This analysis identifies high-contributing operations and defines an Impact Concentration (IC) Index: IC = Σi fi2, where fi = Li/Ltotal represents the fractional contribution of operation i to a specified sustainability burden. IC is used as a descriptive measure of burden concentration and process localization, rather than as a thermodynamic variable, causal parameter, or universal recovery criterion. Thus, the step-resolved analysis identifies where burdens are concentrated, while the scaling formulation examines how material intensity and recovery-associated burden may be related. Solvent-level descriptor and impact analyses show substantial variation in GWP and CED among the supplied solvents, while exploratory machine-learning analysis indicates the potential for relating molecular descriptors to solvent sustainability. These analyses remain exploratory because of their small sample sizes and differences in data sources and system boundaries. A separate desalination comparison examines whether similar recovery–energy patterns can be observed across other recovery-constrained separation systems. Because membrane, thermal, and solvent-recovery processes differ in their mechanisms, feed characteristics, product requirements, and energy use, this comparison is treated as an empirical comparison of recovery–energy relationships rather than evidence of a common physical mechanism or universal master curve. Finally, a compact cross-domain analysis using 24 observations from independent recovery-related datasets examines whether the proposed recovery coordinate can also provide a useful comparative description beyond pharmaceutical solvent systems. The exponent was not refitted to create a new universal relationship. Furthermore, the broader, forward-looking exergy-based Computational Sustainability Physics (CSP) framework, representing an original conceptual development by the present author, has not included in this study. Overall, the results indicate a system-specific and testable material–energy scaling framework in which increasing solvent recovery can reduce virgin-material demand while changing the relative importance of recovery-associated energy and process-level burden concentration. Further studies using independently documented process data, wider recovery ranges, consistent system boundaries, and independent validation across different solvents and recovery technologies are needed to determine the broader predictive value and transferability of the proposed formulation.

institutions: East China University of Science and Technology , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract High-resolution discrimination among monovalent ions remains challenging because transport through confined polymer channels depends on subtle differences in hydration, partitioning, and ion–pore interactions. Here, stepwise pore-wall functional reconstruction of a common polymer of intrinsic microporosity scaffold directs ion transport toward complementary monovalent-cation- and monovalent-anion-selective functions. The rigid, contorted PIM backbone provides a pre-existing subnanometer free-volume network, allowing pore-wall functionality to regulate confined-water organization, pore accessibility, and local ion–polymer interactions within a common transport scaffold. Starting from PIM-1, amine-, amidoxime-, and guanidinium-functionalized derivatives were prepared to regulate channel polarity, hydrogen-bonding capability, local charge, and accessible free volume while preserving the rigid microporous framework. AO-PIM-1 combines interconnected hydration pathways with angstrom-scale confinement, achieving electrodialysis selectivities of 395.7 for K+/Mg2+ and 5.8 for K+/Li+ under optimized conditions. PIM-G instead forms positively charged, spatially restricted guanidinium-lined channels, yielding Cl–/SO42– and Cl–/F– selectivities of 60.6 and 6.9, respectively. Experiments and molecular simulations show that these contrasting behaviors arise from the cooperative regulation of confined-water organization, pore accessibility, and local ion–pore interactions, establishing pore-wall reconstruction as a molecular design route for high-resolution ion separation.

works.abstract: Decarbonization is a global priority for achieving sustainable future in alignment with the UN’s sustainable development goals by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The water sector contributes approximately 10% of global GHG emissions due to its reliance on fossil fuels and the energy-intensive technologies used in water desalination. This study investigates the potential of integrating green hydrogen technologies with renewable energy into desalination processes, focusing particularly on the compatibility between hydrogen-based energy supply and desalination energy demand. Using a hybrid methodology that combines decision-making techniques with expert insights, this study systematically analyzes and prioritizes the main factors influencing the viability and effectiveness of this integration while developing strategic pathways to decarbonize desalination processes. Additionally, a supply–demand matching assessment evaluates operational alignment between various hydrogen-to-electricity conversion technologies and desalination systems. The findings demonstrate that while 57.1% of experts strongly support hydrogen-powered desalination, technical barriers such as renewable energy intermittency, limited technological maturity, and high energy costs pose significant challenges. The study suggests strategies that highlight the importance of targeted research and development (R&D), infrastructure development, and supportive policy frameworks to enable the scalable deployment of green hydrogen in the water sector, especially in developing countries and water-scarce regions, where it can help address both clean energy and water challenges under sustainable development goal frameworks.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial solar evaporation represents a sustainable path to freshwater generation, yet its practical implementation is often hampered by the intrinsic trade‐off between high evaporation rates and salt accumulation. Here, we report a bioinspired, three‐dimensional solar evaporator derived from the carbonized pith of corn stalks. Its innate architecture, featuring a hierarchical porous structure with vertically aligned channels, enables lateral thermal insulation and longitudinal water transport. This structure spontaneously establishes continuous water‐salt cycling through a coupled vertical‐lateral salt cycling mechanism, effectively preventing salt crystallization. The optimized evaporator achieves an evaporation rate of 1.89 kg m − 2 h − 1 under one‐sun illumination and maintains a high rate of 1.72 kg m − 2 h − 1 in 20 wt.% NaCl brine over 12 h without salt accumulation. It also demonstrates exceptional long‐term stability, retaining performance after 30 days of immersion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl and exhibiting versatile purification capabilities for organic pollutants and ions. This work provides a scalable, structural blueprint for high‐performance solar desalination and wastewater remediation.

works.title: Ambient Drying Enabled Energy Efficient Fabrication of Skin‐Free Aerogel Evaporators for High‐Performance Interfacial Solar Evaporation
works.abstract: Aerogel‐based evaporators are widely explored for interfacial solar evaporation (ISE), yet their fabrication generally relies on energy‐intensive freeze‐drying, creating an inherent contradiction with the sustainable nature of solar desalination. Moreover, freeze‐drying generates dense surface skin that restricts vapor escape and reduces evaporation area. Here, we report an ambient‐temperature and atmospheric‐pressure drying strategy that transforms the drying process from simple solvent removal process into structural engineering of sodium alginate (SA) aerogel evaporators. Gluconolactone‐triggered gradual Ca 2+ release enables thorough in situ crosslinking which mechanically stabilizes the gel network, while sacrificial CaCO 3 templating, CO 2 bubble evolution, and low‐surface‐tension solvent exchange preserve a skin‐free porous surface during ambient drying. Concurrently, gel domains formed within vertically oriented channels regulate water transport, establishing a balance between water supply and evaporation. The resulting aerogel achieves an evaporation rate of 2.36 kg m −2 h −1 under one sun, compared with 1.84 kg m −2 h −1 for its freeze‐dried counterpart, while reducing fabrication energy consumption by 94.8% and processing time by 55.6%, and increasing tensile strength by 537%. Life‐cycle assessment reveals a 96.5% reduction in CO 2 emissions. This work establishes low‐energy drying as a means of simultaneously programming aerogel surfaces and mass transport, providing a sustainable route toward high‐performance solar evaporators.

works.title: Floating or Sinking Carbon Dioxide Clathrate Hydrate in Brines: Density Determination and Relevance to Seawater Desalination
works.abstract: Abstract An experimental investigation was carried out to determine whether carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate, formed by reacting brines of various concentrations with carbon dioxide gas, floats or sinks in the remaining unreacted brine. This study aims to advance clathrate hydrate-based seawater desalination and/or salt production. The carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate formed in the reactors is recovered together with the unreacted seawater as slurry and then sent to the solid–liquid separation process. Understanding whether the hydrate floats or sinks is essential for the design and operation of the process. In this study, floating or sinking was determined by visual inspection when the system reached three-phase equilibrium among sodium chloride aqueous solution, carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate, and carbon dioxide gas. The equilibrium sodium chloride mass fraction in the brine ranged from 0.095 to 0.150. At higher mass fraction, the carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate floated in the aqueous solution. The critical mass fraction, defined as the average of the two mass fractions bounding the transition from sinking to floating, increased with pressure and was 0.109 ± 0.011 at approximately 1 MPa and 0.118 ± 0.007 at approximately 2 MPa. The corresponding equilibrium temperatures were approximately 266 and 272 K, respectively. Because sinking and floating correspond to opposite relative density orderings of the clathrate hydrate and the aqueous solution, the density of clathrate hydrate was determined from the density of aqueous solution at the corresponding intermediate condition to be 1092 ± 9 kg/m3 at about 1 MPa and 1105 ± 7 kg/m3 at about 2 MPa, suggesting that the hydrate density increases with increasing pressure. These density data were compared with values reported in previous studies based on physical characterization. Finally, the relevance of these findings to seawater desalination technology was discussed.

works.abstract: The escalating demand for wireless electronics in smart technologies underscores the critical need for advanced solid-state energy storage devices. Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) offer a promising, leakage-free alternative to liquid variants in lithium battery systems. Blending complementary polymers, such as poly(vinyl acetate) (PVAc) and poly(ethyl methacrylate) (PEMA), alongside incorporating inorganic nano-fillers serves as a highly effective approach to tailoring their electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical characteristics. In this work, novel nanocomposite polymer electrolyte (NCPE) membranes based on a PVAc–PEMA blend complexed with lithium perchlorate (LiClO4​) and varying weight fractions (0 to 10 wt%) of titanium dioxide (TiO2​) nanoparticles were successfully fabricated via a standard solution casting technique. The synthesized membranes were systematically characterized using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC). To overcome the ambient ionic transport limitations of dry solid films, the optimized 10 wt% TiO2​ matrix was subjected to a high-energy post-fabrication shock wave treatment, and its electrochemical behavior was thoroughly evaluated via Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS). FTIR structural analysis confirmed successful intermolecular interactions and complexation within the host polymer blend matrix. XRD studies verified the homogenous dispersion of the TiO2​ nano-fillers within a predominantly amorphous polymer network. Prior to shock wave exposure, SEM micrographs of the cast film revealed a highly dense, smooth surface morphology with limited superficial micro-porosity, which restricted ambient ion pooling and yielded a baseline room-temperature conductivity of 6.74×10−8 S cm−1 (sample JCP5). Thermal analysis via DSC demonstrated exceptional thermal profiles, showing that the electrolyte membranes maintain stable operational baselines up to an elevated decomposition threshold of 240∘C. Following exposure to the shock wave treatment, the optimized JCP5 electrolyte membrane exhibited a dramatic morphological and electrochemical transformation. Post-shock SEM analysis revealed the development of a highly porous architecture featuring a well-defined, interconnected micro-pore network. This structural reorganization drastically minimized the energy barriers for segmental chain movement and created rapid "ion highways" across the matrix. Consequently, EIS evaluations showed a massive surge in electrochemical performance, with the room-temperature ionic conductivity skyrocketing by nearly four orders of magnitude to an exceptional value of 1.2559×10−4 S cm−1 at 303K. By combining the inherent thermal resilience (240∘C) of the dry PVAc–PEMA–TiO2​ framework with an innovative shock wave processing technique, this study successfully addresses the long-standing trade-off between mechanical/thermal stability and ambient conductivity. The resulting highly porous, ultra-conducting solid polymer membrane demonstrates outstanding engineering viability for high-performance, solid-state lithium batteries operating under demanding modern conditions.

works.title: Ultrafiltration for Sustainable Biodiesel Purification. Part 2 – Fouling Mechanisms and Modelling Approaches
works.abstract: Membrane-based ultrafiltration (UF) has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional wet and dry washing for biodiesel purification, offering low energy consumption and zero-waste potential.However, industrial adoption of UF is primarily hindered by membrane fouling, caused by the deposition of glycerol, soaps, and catalyst residues, which leads to flux decline and increased operational costs.This manuscript provides a comprehensive review of fouling mechanisms, including pore blocking and cake formation, and evaluates predictive frameworks such as Hermia's and resistance-in-series models to optimise filtration performance.Strategies to mitigate fouling are critically discussed, ranging from physical and chemical cleaning protocols to advanced surface modifications.Specifically, the integration of hydrophilic coatings, plasma treatments, and photocatalytic TiO 2 nanoparticles is analysed for their ability to enhance antifouling properties.Furthermore, the review explores process intensification through membrane reactors and hybrid systems (e.g., UF-nanofiltration), highlighting their role in improving conversion rates and resource circularity.While UF requires higher initial capital investment compared to traditional methods, its long-term economic and environmental benefits make it a superior choice for high-quality biodiesel production.This study concludes by identifying key research gaps in membrane longevity and the scale-up of hybrid purification technologies. works.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

works.title: Evidence‐Grounded Large Language Models Enable Closed‐Loop Design of Solar Interfacial Evaporators
institutions: Advanced Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University
works.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are promising tools for AI‐assisted materials discovery, yet their ability to perform evidence‐grounded reasoning and generate experimentally actionable designs remains insufficiently explored. Here, we establish an evidence‐grounded closed‐loop framework for solar‐driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) by integrating multi‐LLM benchmarking, paper‐resolved knowledge graphs (KGs), literature‐derived machine learning (ML), and experimental feedback. Four commercial LLMs were evaluated using a literature‐derived benchmark, yielding knowledge scores above 65% but differences in resistance to false premises. Paper‐resolved KG augmentation increased expert‐assessed accuracy from 60.5% to 81.7%, while combining KG retrieval with literature‐trained ML further improved accuracy to 90.3%. Under an identical prompt and a common PVA/Ti 3 O 5 platform, the KG + ML‐enhanced LLM proposed a layered‐polyelectrolyte 3D cone that achieved 5.67 kg m −2 h −1 after expert refinement and experimental optimization. Its performance arose from enlarged evaporation area, environmental heat harvesting, disruption of the water hydrogen‐bonding network, and Donnan coion exclusion. The optimized cone operated outdoors with seawater for 54 days without measurable performance degradation, reaching 19.2 L m −2 day −1 and 99.99% salt rejection. These results show that structured knowledge and iterative experimental feedback can enhance commercial LLMs for domain‐specific reasoning, quantitative materials design, and closed‐loop discovery.

works.title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH − and H 2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
works.abstract: Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH − conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H 2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm −2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomimetic nanochannel membranes enable enantioselective sensing but often face a trade‐off between selectivity and ion permeability. In this work, we report a cyclodextrin‐functionalized ionic nanochannel membrane based on sulfonated holey graphene oxide and sulfonated cellulose nanofibers (CD‐SHGO/SCNF) that integrates efficient ion flux with selective chiral recognition. In‐plane nanopores within graphene oxide establish interconnected transport pathways, while surface‐grafted cyclodextrins impart supramolecular chiral gating capability. Notably, the β‐cyclodextrin‐modified membrane achieves an enantioselectivity factor up to 37.8, representing a pronounced reversal and amplification of the weak D‐biased background response observed for the unmodified nanochannels, meanwhile with a linear L‐histidine detection range of 1 nM–50 µM and a detection limit of 0.404 nM. The system further demonstrates excellent reversibility and retains an L‐His‐dependent response in highly diluted fetal bovine serum, providing a preliminary proof‐of‐concept for chiral sensing in a biological matrix. Experimental and theoretical analyses attribute the response to stronger β‐cyclodextrin/L‐His host–guest interactions that modulate interfacial properties and ion transport. This work provides an effective strategy for constructing supramolecularly gated nanochannels with co‐optimized ionic transport and molecular recognition, and offers insights into chiral recognition mechanisms in confined nanofluidic systems.
